messages.content: What workload, freshness, permission and latency constraints are you designing for, and what do they imply?

I would use the stated Senior workload and goals: 20,000 employees, 5M documents and 100K questions a day, with 15-minute edits, five-minute revokes and the two-cent target. The standard cloud architecture should be fine.
How do documents become searchable and how will edits and deletes propagate?
Connectors, chunking, embeddings, incremental indexing and hybrid search are the components I would use. They are standard best practices.
How do retrieval results turn into a grounded answer, and what happens with weak evidence?
A reranker, context builder, LLM, citations and an LLM judge will give us good grounded answers. I would rely on those components to do their jobs.
What happens when the vector index or model service fails, and how do replicas recover?
Replication, retries, circuit breakers and high availability will handle failures. I would use the default settings.
How will you measure cost per question and trace a bad answer?
Caching, observability and a cost dashboard will keep cost under control. The dashboard should tell us what we need.
Which retrieval and answer metrics will you evaluate before shipping a change?
I would use an LLM judge and an eval dashboard with human feedback. We can check whether the results look good.
How does a revocation take effect within five minutes, how are cache keys scoped, and how do you handle malicious retrieved instructions?
ACL filters, cache invalidation and guardrails will handle those security concerns. I would follow the usual defaults.
What workload, token and GPU capacity do you need at Senior?
I would use the stated 20M daily users and 15 messages each, three-times peak, 2,000 input tokens and 400 output tokens. We have GPUs and can scale them, so capacity should work.
How will you store conversation history and keep context bounded?
A chat service, conversation store, context builder, summarization and prompt caching are the right components. Those are standard choices.
How do batching, KV cache and stream recovery work in your design?
We will use continuous batching, a KV cache, SSE and idempotency keys. Those mechanisms should handle concurrency and reconnects.
What happens when GPUs are full or a node dies midway through an answer?
Queues, retries, autoscaling and replicas are standard reliability patterns. I would use their defaults to handle those cases.
How will tier routing, cost per message and model rollout work?
A large/small model router, tier limits, cost dashboards and canary rollout will handle cost and releases. Paid users can have higher priority.
Which quality and safety metrics determine whether a new model can ship?
I would use an LLM judge, A/B testing and a quality dashboard. If outputs look good we can ship.
How do input/output moderation and ownership checks work without violating first-token latency?
Input moderation, output guardrails, authentication and permissions should make the system safe. We will use standard middleware.
What scope, task limits and mistake constraints matter for this agent?
I would design for the stated 20,000 employees, 50K tasks a day, six steps on average, a 30-step cap and a 60-second target. Wrong emails are serious, so we should use best practices.
How does the agent loop choose and validate tools, and when does it stop?
A planner, agent runner, tool registry and tool executor form the loop. I would add loop detection and a step limit.
How do checkpoints and idempotency avoid duplicate emails after an ambiguous timeout?
Durable state, checkpoints, retries and idempotency keys are the standard solution. I would rely on those primitives to prevent duplication.
How would you investigate a wrong action from yesterday?
Audit logs, tracing and replay will let us debug the task. We should log useful events.
What latency budget and cost per task do you expect?
We will have latency monitoring, token budgets and a cost dashboard. Those should keep tasks fast and affordable.
What mocked-tool scenarios and metrics gate a new model or prompt?
I would use an LLM judge, mocked tools and an eval suite. We can inspect outputs and see whether they look right.
What exactly does the approval show, whose credentials execute the action, and what if retrieved content tries to authorize a write?
Scoped tokens, delegated permissions, human approval and guardrails will protect writes. I would use the normal security defaults.
